auditor_value: (a) car frame: parabola in the horizontal floor plane, x_rel = -2.5 t^2 (backward along i), z_rel = 10 t, so x_rel = -z_rel^2/40; (b) ground frame: straight line at constant 10 m/s along k

findings.quote: in the ground frame the object moves in a straight line at constant 20 m/s along k̂
findings.note: The question gives the sideways speed as 10 m/s, and the solution itself uses 10 m/s in steps[0] and steps[2] (z_rel = 10t). The ground-frame speed is the unchanged initial speed, 10 m/s; 20 m/s appears nowhere in the question.
findings.fix: in the ground frame the object moves in a straight line at constant 10 m/s along k̂

findings.note: From steps[2], z_rel = 10t, so t = z_rel/10, not z_rel/20. The printed equation is false for this question (it would need a 20 m/s speed).

notes: The mass (2 kg) and g = 10 given in the question are not needed for the path: on a frictionless floor the normal force balances the weight and the mass cancels, so not using them is not a defect. The car-frame parabola and the ground-frame straight line (the shape answers) agree with mine; only the speed value is wrong.
